title: Question 5
stem:
Two small solid metal spheres A and B have equal radii and are in a vacuum. Their centres are
15 cm apart.
Sphere A has charge +3.0 pC and sphere B has charge +12 pC. The arrangement is illustrated in
Fig. 5.1.
Point P lies on the line joining the centres of the spheres and is a distance of 5.0 cm from the
centre of sphere A.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest why the electric field strength in both spheres is zero.

markscheme_points.text: in an electric field, charges (in a conductor) would move
no movement of charge so zero field strength or charge moves until F = 0 / E = 0
or charges in metal do not move (B1) no (resultant) force on charges so no (electric) field

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Show that the electric field strength is zero at point P. Explain your working.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
at P, EA = (3.0 × 10-12) / [4πε0(5.0 × 10-2)2] (= 10.79 N C-1); at P, EB = (12 × 10-12) / [4πε0(10 × 10-2)2] (= 10.79 N C-1); or (3.0 × 10-12) / [4πε0(5.0 × 10-2)2] - (12 × 10-12) / [4πε0(10 × 10-2)2] = 0 or (3.0 × 10-12) / [4πε0(5.0 × 10-2)2] = (12 × 10-12) / [4πε0(10 × 10-2)2] (M2) fields due to charged spheres are (equal and) opposite in direction, so E = 0
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the electric potential at point P.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
potential = 8.99 × 109 {(3.0 × 10-12) / (5.0 × 10-2) + (12 × 10-12) / (10 × 10-2)}; = 1.62 V
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
A silver-107 nucleus (^{107}
_{47}Ag) has speed v when it is a long distance from point P.
Use your answer in (c) to calculate the minimum value of speed v such that the nucleus can
reach point P.
$speed = m s ^{1} $
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
½mv2 = qV EK = ½ × 107 × 1.66 × 10-27 × v 2; qV = 47 × 1.60 × 10-19 × 1.62; v 2 = 1.37 × 108 v = 1.2 × 104 m s-1
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
